WORKFORCE / SCHOOLS

Housing that helps
you hire teachers.

For school districts, county offices of education and tribal schools.

Furnished private rooms with their own bath and kitchenette, on land your district already owns.

Start a conversationSee the units

THE PROBLEM

Rural districts lose teachers when there is nowhere to live.

A district can make the offer and still lose the hire because there is nothing to rent nearby. Many districts already own land next to a campus or a spare parcel. What they need is housing they can place on it quickly.

HOW DISTRICTS USE IT

A small cluster on district land.

Where
District-owned land next to a campus, or a surplus parcel.
Who
New and visiting teachers, student teachers, specialists and support staff.
Room
Furnished private room, bath pod and kitchenette. Accessible units in the mix.
Owner
The district owns the cluster, or leases it from a housing partner.
Rent
Set by the district.

PAYING FOR IT

Ways districts fund staff housing.

  • Programs

    Federal and state

    Some districts use federal and state housing programs for staff housing.

  • Voters

    Bonds and levies

    Some districts put staff housing in a bond or levy.

  • Partners

    Housing partners

    A housing authority or nonprofit builds on district land and leases rooms to staff.

  • Budget

    Start small

    A few rooms from the district budget, then a larger cluster once they fill.

Program rules on unit size, ownership and rent vary. We check fit on the first call.
